title: Midsegments, Perpendicular Bisectors and Medians
seo_title: Geometry Midsegments, Bisectors and Medians Worksheets (TEKS G.6D)
standard_text: G.6D verify theorems about the relationships in triangles, including midsegments and medians, and apply these relationships to solve problems; G.6A prove equidistance between the endpoints of a segment and points on its perpendicular bisector and apply these relationships to solve problems; G.5C use the constructions of congruent segments, congruent angles, angle bisectors, and perpendicular bisectors to make conjectures about geometric relationships
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.6D, G.6A and G.5C: midsegments, perpendicular and angle bisectors, medians, the centroid and triangle centers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Midsegment = half the third side; centroid splits medians 2 : 1.
key_sub: Points on a perpendicular bisector are equidistant from the endpoints.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A midsegment joins two midpoints. It is parallel to the third side and half as long.
  • Any point on the perpendicular bisector of a segment is the same distance from both endpoints.
  • A median goes from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. The centroid splits each median 2 : 1 from the vertex.
  • Perpendicular bisectors meet at the circumcenter; angle bisectors at the incenter.

Examples

Example

The third side is 18

half of 18

Answer: midsegment 9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Doubling instead of halvingThe midsegment is half the third side.
Using 2 : 1 the wrong wayThe longer part is next to the vertex.
Mixing up the centersAngle bisectors meet at the incenter.

faq.a: Verify theorems about the relationships in triangles, including proof of the Pythagorean Theorem, the sum of interior angles, base angles of isosceles triangles, midsegments, and medians, and apply these relationships to solve problems.
Use the constructions of congruent segments, congruent angles, angle bisectors, and perpendicular bisectors to make conjectures about geometric relationships.
Two-thirds of the way along each median from the vertex.

items.q: The sides of a triangle are 48, 44 and 16. The three midsegments form a smaller triangle. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Each midsegment is half of a side, so the perimeter is half: (48 + 44 + 16) ÷ 2 = 54.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is the center of a circle that touches all three sides?
items.e: The incenter is the center of a circle that touches all three sides.

items.q: A designer wants the largest circle that fits inside a triangular garden. Which center is the circle's center?
items.e: The incenter is the same distance from the three sides (lines). Incenter.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is the same distance from all three vertices?
items.e: The circumcenter is the same distance from all three vertices.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is the same distance from all three sides?
items.e: The incenter is the same distance from all three sides.

items.q: Three towns want a water tower the same distance from each town. Which center should they use?
items.e: The circumcenter is the same distance from the three vertices (points). Circumcenter.

items.q: The perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle meet at which point?
items.e: The perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet at the circumcenter.

items.q: Three friends live at different houses and want to meet at a point equally far from all three. Which center?
items.e: The circumcenter is the same distance from the three vertices (points). Circumcenter.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is the center of a circle through all three vertices?
items.e: The circumcenter is the center of a circle through all three vertices.

items.q: In an equilateral triangle, how are the four centers placed?
c: They are all the same point
Two are inside and two are outside
items.e: Every bisector, median and altitude is the same line in an equilateral triangle. They are all the same point.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is 2/3 of the way from each vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side?
items.e: The centroid is 2/3 of the way from each vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

items.q: The altitudes of a triangle meet at which point?
items.e: The altitudes meet at the orthocenter.

items.q: Where is the circumcenter of a right triangle?
c: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse
items.e: The hypotenuse is a diameter of the circle through the three vertices. At the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

items.q: A park ranger wants a lookout the same distance from three straight roads that form a triangle. Which center?
items.e: The incenter is the same distance from the three sides (lines). Incenter.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is where the heights meet?
items.e: The orthocenter is where the heights meet.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is where the lines through each vertex perpendicular to the opposite side meet?
items.e: The orthocenter is where the lines through each vertex perpendicular to the opposite side meet.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is the balance point of the triangle?
items.e: The centroid is the balance point of the triangle.

items.q: The medians of a triangle meet at which point?
items.e: The medians meet at the centroid.

items.q: Where is the circumcenter of an obtuse triangle?
items.e: The perpendicular bisectors meet outside, beyond the longest side. Outside the triangle.

items.q: Where is the orthocenter of a right triangle?
c: At the vertex of the right angle
At the midpoint of the hypotenuse
items.e: The two legs are altitudes, and they meet at the right angle. At the vertex of the right angle.

items.q: A student wants to balance a triangular piece of cardboard on a pencil tip. Which center?
items.e: The centroid is the balance point. Centroid.
